Seduva Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Seduva was home to one of the most beautiful Aron Kodesh in Lithuania, housed in a synagogue inaugurated by the Chevra Kadisha in 1866, and the town held the oldest Torah scroll in the country. Nearly burned to the ground during WWI, the town rebuilt, though its Jewish population never recovered its 1880 peak of 2,386. Remarkably, all of the town's Jewish youth were reported to speak and write Hebrew. In August 1941, 664 Seduva residents were murdered in two separate massacres, at Liaudiskiai forest and Pakuteniai village; a monument to all the town's Jewish residents was erected in 2015. This cemetery, established in the first half of the 18th century, fell into disrepair after the Holocaust and through the Soviet era, making the fate of many tombstones difficult to trace. A major cleanup from 2013 to 2014 discovered and catalogued over 800 headstones, 400 of them identifiable, with burials dating from 1779-80 to 1932; a memorial in the shape of a Star of David, built from fragments of former gravestones, now stands on the site.
